Partnership work strengthened in various spaces at the global level that speaks to the power of deepened movement-building to build power through political and civic engagement and participation, create evidence that informs advocacy, and collectively strategize and co-create joint political agendas. 1) A strengthened alliance which is the WHRDIC network of global human rights defenders and WRO members. This alliance can be categorized as a coalition type of alliance. The second grant resulted in strengthening 15 grantee partners and 9 practitioners across 10 countries. These alliances can be categorized as partnerships for research and documentation. Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism’s support revitalized and strengthened the WHRDIC network. This implies that the capacity developed includes governance, strategic planning, operations, engagement with UN mechanisms, advocacy, and social media campaigns. 2) In response to increasing repressive governments and contexts due to expanding authoritarianism and anti-rights movement that pose more threats to civic space and WHRDs and structurally excluded activists and community members, UAF FA partnered and strengthened partnerships with 15 grantee partners and 9 practitioners across 10 countries who contributed to research and documentation of their experiences and resources on reprisals. This deepened UAF FA's understanding of contexts along with the types of reprisals and presence of resources and infrastructure (or lack of resources and infrastructure needed) to support WHRDs, WROs and feminist movements as they face retribution for their human rights activism. UAF FA is building out a microsite that provides resources for WHRDs, WROs and feminist activists who face reprisals to help plan, manage and partner with others. We are also conducting a social media campaign to highlight these issues. UAF FA will continue to partner with our grantees, advisors and participants who contributed to the report via advocacy opportunities, grant support and networking connections. 3) Through a partnership btw Women Enabled International (WEI) and UAF for Feminst Activisim (UAF FA) a grant supported research and documentation work of a global WRO (Women Enabled International - WEI) working to enhance and protect through advocacy, policy and norm change regional mappings of WHRDs working at the intersection of disabilty and gender justice. This funding enabled WEI to carry out their organizational goals to create evidence for field-building and advocacy to advance disability justice and rights, create advocacy opportunities and build more inclusive communities. WEI's research report contributed to the institutional strengthening of UAF FA's grantmaking and partnership building, as well as deepened our relationship and alliance with WEI. WEI also strengthened and deepened its partnership with UAF grantees, advisors and other WROs and activists working on DJ issues through interviewing and documenting as part of their research on DJ issues across the SWANA, Eastern Europe, Balkans and Central Asia regions. This culminated in 2024, at CSW a joint session co-hosted by WEI and UAF FA with other partners, including CMI!, targeting donors and policymakers.

With CMI funding, a delegation of sex workers from Sexual Rights Initiative (SRI) and Global Network of Sex Work Projects (NSWP) from many countries across different regions were supported to engage at the Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva in June and October 2024. The result of advocacy engagement in these spaces strengthened collaboration with allies and increased their visibility and messaging/advocacy. This included working closely with organisations like Amnesty International, WO=MEN, MamaCash, and others, the delegation bolstered its messaging through joint programming, including side events and strategic discussions. The side event "Decriminalising Sex Work: A Human Rights Imperative" was well attended and a question about the side event was even posed to the Special Rapporteur on violence against wome (SP VAW) n during a press conference organised by the mandate holder to launch her report. The communications campaign played a crucial role in raising awareness of sex workers’rights and challenging harmful narratives and ideas. The high level of engagement across multiple platforms helped to disseminate the delegation’s key messages widely, reaching stakeholders across different sectors and reinforcing the call for decriminalisation. These advocacy spaces and the opportunity to speak out against the harmful narratives and ideas from the report put out by the SP on VAW.

actual.value: Follow up and accountability process around the Action coalition 6 as well as the GEF more broadly.

comment.narrative: These are examples of what UAF FA has accomplished in partnership with global coalitions. 1)Followed up on action coalition and GEF commitments. Provided feedback and recommendations to equip policymakers and hold them accountable for post-GEF accountability. Coordinated with Prospera, CMI, the Feminist Generation Consortium, and Spotlight to develop and streamline demands and strategies around the GEF and beyond. With Prospera, UAF FA was part of the group who drafted the Call for Action from Women’s Funds. Voted for Women's Funds to be on the Global Alliance steering committee, in which Mama Cash is part of this committee. 2)UAF FA worked with CMI partners to organize a GPP Shimmering Solidarity session on Funding feminist movements so they can thrive. The session was well attended and provided concrete recommendations to funders on how to better support feminist movements in sustainable and holistic ways. UAF FA co-organized a GPP Shimmering Solidarity session on Resourcing Collective Care for Intersectional Feminist and Queer Movements in The North Caucasus and Central Asia. The session was well attended and participants were engaged and moved by the honest, vulnerable, and deeply personal and political conversation, which was revolutionary in a philanthropic space. Speakers reflected on what trauma-informed collective care means in these regions and shared specific recommendations from activist movements to guide donors’ programs and advocacy.

2022 data:1) With Prospera, UAF FA joined the Alliance for Feminist Movements which drafted the Call for Action from Women’s Funds. UAF FA staff voted for Women's Funds to be on the Alliance steering committee, in which Mama Cash is part of this committee. Donors have established an inclusive and diverse multi-stakeholder mechanism through which women's funds and WROs can more effectively influence and participate in decision making and in turn improve the quantity and quality of funds going to feminist movements, especially grassroots organizations.2) UAF FA’s continued work with Spotlight advocacy has contributed to helping shift the funding culture and practices of the UN, EU, and other funders, providing concrete and in-depth recommendations so more and better money reaches frontline feminist movements. Donors have integrated recommendations and shifted their policies and practices to better support feminist movements. The EU integrated our key recommendations, including prioritizing larger flexible funds for regional networks that include grassroots groups, and they have been considering longer term ways to shift their funding modalities, including potentially through Women’s Funds, so they can better reach grassroots groups. We obtained approval for payment for National and Regional Civil Society Reference Group members to compensate them for their time and work to help strengthen Spotlight. Spotlight’s submitted a joint application to the EU for with other UN agencies for follow up funding to end GBV that integrated all our edits, including regarding flexible funds for grassroots groups.2023 data:Support from UAF FA bolstered the impact of WHRDIC's lobbying and advocacy work that resulted in the following: 1) The UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights defenders, Mary Lawlor, and WHRDs met through co-facilitated consultations between the across different regions that resulted in recommendations to be included in next report to the UN General Assembly about the challenges faced by WHRDs in working in conflict, post-conflict or crisis-affected settings. 2) As the result of how WHRDIC engaged members in the WHRD Advocacy week by bringing diverse WHRDs to the 54th session of the Human Rights Council in Geneva and training them on how to engage with the HRs Council, policy-makers, donors, international NGOs, and other WHRDs met with the WHRDIC coalition during the WHRD Advocacy week. 3) Other activities included the launch of social media campaign highlighting human rights violations that WHRDs face, and this was on Noor's website, a global feminist and movement-driven think-and-do tank. With a bolstered infrastructure now in place, the WHRDIC is well-positioned for sustainability and greater impact in 2024 and beyond.

The reporting indicator is unique, considering it takes a long time to influence laws, policies and strategies used at the national level. This will be a 5-year target. The achievement of laws and policies will be counted only once
